CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH RAI K  ORAL ORDER

This petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 to quash the proceedings in Crl.Misc.No.275/2023 pending on the file of Civil Judge & JMFC, Shahapur against the petitioners by the respondent for the offences under Sections 9, 12, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 of Domestic Violence Act (for brevity "D.V. Act").
2.
The factual matrix of the case is that petitioner No.1-Shivaputra married respondent-Sashikala prior to 12 NC: 2026:KHC-K:763 HC-KAR years from 31.03.2023.
After the marriage, they both stayed together and out of the wedlock, they begotten three children.
Later, petitioner No.1-husband started to suspect the fidelity of the respondent and as such, started to harass her both physically and mentally.
The other petitioners i.e. accused No.2 to 6 also instigated accused No.1 and thereby abused the respondent and assaulted her.
It is further stated that, petitioner No.1 was addicted for bad vices and was continuously harassing her.
As such, she lodged a complaint before the Gurumitkal Police against the petitioners.

Shivaputra And Ors vs Shashikala on 30 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79737440/
2 3.
On the strength of the said complaint, FIR was registered in Crime No.166/2022.
Thereafter, the respondent was thrown out from the matrimonial home and she along with the children started to reside in her parental house.
Hence she filed Criminal Miscellaneous Petition before the Civil Judge and JMFC, Shahapur at Yadgir, for the Domestic Violence caused against her.
Based on her complaint, the learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offences and issued summons to the petitioners.
Hence this petition.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:763 HC-KAR 4.

It is stated in the petition filed before the trial Court that petitioner No.1 i.e., husband of respondent, alone, allegedly harassed the respondent and the other petitioners i.e., accused No.2 to 6 are no way connected to the alleged harassment meted out by petitioner No.1.

It is further stated that the relief claimed by the respondent is only in respect to the monetary relief and for the same,
petitioner No.1 i.e., the husband is alone liable to pay.
It is also contented that the other relief claimed in the petition that not to alienate the movable and immovable property belonging to the petitioners is not sustainable under law.
For the said relief, the respondent has to approach the Civil Court.

In such circumstance, it is stated that the proceedings initiated under the provisions of 12, 9,
18, 19, 20, 21, 22 of Domestic Violence Act is liable to be quashed.
5. Though the notice is served to the respondent, she remained absent.
6. I have carefully perused the documents available on record.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:763 HC-KAR 7.
As could be gathered from records, the relationship between the petitioners and respondent is not in dispute.
It is stated in the petition filed by the respondent under the D.V. Act that her husband-petitioner No.1 was addicted to bad vices and he used to harass her both physically and mentally.
As such, she lodged the complaint before the Gurumitkal police, which was registered in a Crime No.166/2022.

The petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are the sister-in-law and other close relatives of petitioner No.1 and they are no way connected for the prayer made in the petition filed by respondent before the trial Court.

The monetary relief and other reliefs claimed by the respondent in the petition is liable to be complied with by husband of respondent i.e., petitioner No.1.
8.

In such circumstance, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Petition No.3578/2022 dated 28.06.2024 has held that, if prima facie case has not been made out against the other family members, except the husband, they cannot be roped in the criminal case by relying on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SHYAMLAL DEVDA v. PARIMALA reported in 2020 (3) SCC 2014, wherein paragraph Nos.8 and 9 reads as under:
NC: 2026:KHC-K:763 HC-KAR ".... .... ....
8.

In terms of Section 18 of the Act, intention of the legislature is to provide more protection to Shivaputra And Ors vs Shashikala on 30 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79737440/

sentences.text: Section 20 of the Act empowers the court to order for monetary relief to the "aggrieved party".

When acts of domestic violence are alleged, before issuing notice,
the court has to be prima facie satisfied that there have been instances of domestic violence.
9. In the present case, the respondent has made allegations of domestic violence against fourteen appellants.
Appellant 14 is the husband and Appellants 1 and 2 are the parents-in-law of the respondent.
All other appellants are relatives of parents-in-law of the respondent.
Appellants 3, 5, 9, 11 and 12 are the brothers of father-in-law of the respondent.

Appellants 4, 6 and 10 are the wives of Appellants 3,
5 and 9 respectively.
Appellants 7 and 8 are the parents of Appellant 1.
Appellants 1 to 6 and 14 are residents of Chennai.
Appellants 7 to 10 are the residents of the State of Rajasthan and Appellants 11 to 13 are the residents of the State of Gujarat.
Admittedly, the matrimonial house of the respondent and Appellant 1 has been at Chennai.

Insofar as Appellant 14 husband of the respondent and Appellants 1 and 2 parents-in-law, there are averments of alleged domestic violence alleging that they have taken away the jewellery of the respondent gifted to her by her father during marriage and the alleged acts of harassment to the respondent.
There are no specific allegations as to how other relatives of Appellant 14 have caused the acts of domestic violence.
It is also not known as to how other relatives who are residents of Gujarat and Rajasthan can be held responsible for award of monetary relief to the respondent.
The High Court was not right in saying that there was prima facie NC: 2026:KHC-K:763 HC-KAR case against the other Appellants 3 to 13.
Since there are no specific allegations against Appellants 3 to 13, the criminal case of domestic violence against them cannot be continued and is liable to be quashed.

9. Further in para-12 and 13 of the judgment of the co-ordinate bench held as under:
"12.

The High Court of Andhra Pradesh, following the judgment of the Apex Court in SHYAMLAL DEVDA'S case supra, in the case of MORA v. STATE OF AP5 holds that the judgment in SHYAMLAL DEVADA'S case did not specifically decide maintainability, but there is no bar of exercise of power of a Court under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. in a proceeding under the Act.

The High Court has held as follows:
"9.

On the other hand, in case of Shyamlal Devda v. Parimala, (2020) 3 SCC 14,
Hon'ble Apex Court has set aside the order passed by the High Court wherein the proceedings under DV Act were not quashed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Though this judgment also does not specifically decide applicability of Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to DV Act, however,
the said judgment more than sufficiently indicates that there is no bar to exercise powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to the proceeding under DV Act."

sentences.text: Now coming to the pivotal question whether this court can exercise jurisdiction under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, to set at naught the proceedings initiated by the respondent under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, it is apposite to refer the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State Of Haryana referred supra, where it was held that the Court exercising jurisdiction is not shorn of the power under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India and whenever Court is confronted with a situation where the provision of any penal law is abused, it would unhesitatingly exercise jurisdiction to set at naught such proceeding.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
12. In the case on hand, though it is contended that the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kamatchi supra held that under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure,
the High Court cannot exercise jurisdiction to quash the proceedings under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005, in the instant case, the proceedings before the Trial Court has moved on from the stage of issuing notice.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The consequence of non- compliance of an order under Sections 21 and 22 is provided in Section 31 of the Act of 2005, which reads as follows :
"31. Penalty for breach of protection order by respondent.--
NC: 2026:KHC-K:763 HC-KAR (1) A breach of protection order, or of an interim protection order, by the respondent shall be an offence under this Act and shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both.
(2) The offence under sub- section (1) shall as far as practicable be tried by the Magistrate who had passed the order, the breach of which has been alleged to have been caused by the accused.

(3) While framing charges under sub-section (1), the Magistrate may also frame charges under section 498A of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) or any other provision of that Code or the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (28 of 1961), as the case may be, if the facts disclose the commission of an offence under those provisions."
13.
Therefore, it cannot be held that the provisions under the PWDV Act 2005 are civil in nature.

Therefore, when the Court is confronted with a false case or a case which does not constitute domestic violence as defined under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence act 2005, the Shivaputra And Ors vs Shashikala on 30 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79737440/
5 same cannot continue, as that would result in nuisance and harassment of the petitioner.

Hence, in my considered opinion, the proceedings against petitioner Nos.2 to 6 is an abuse of process of Court.
However, the proceedings against petitioner No.1 is liable to be continued.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The petition is allowed-in-part.

ii. The proceedings in Crl.Misc.No.275/2023, pending on the file of Civil Judge &
JMFC, Shahapur at Yadgir, is quashed in respect of petitioner Nos.2 to 6 i.e.,
respondent Nos.2 to 6 before the Trial Court.
